messages:
anna: Quick Q — ran into a 413 on /v1/embeddings. Client sent ~2k vectors (1536 dims) base64-packed, ~14MB body. Are we clear on per-request byte limit + how we handle mixed dims?

mike: We do have a 10MB gateway limit (nginx). Not super visible in the public docs. For dims we only validate per-item, not per-request mixing right now.

devon: Ideally the endpoint can accept mixed dims and internally shard into homogeneous batches so the runtime can pick kernels/quant paths. That reduces client work but adds router complexity.

jen: Can we add a lightweight header like `X-Embed-Dims` so the router knows batch strategy before full parse? We already use similar heuristics for other routes.

anna: Header seems reasonable. Also want telemetry when we split: how many shards, items per shard, total bytes.

mike: +1. Emit `embed.request.item_count`, `embed.request.shard_count`, `embed.request.bytes`. Also a `embed.request.dim_histogram` for the request.

devon: Implementation note: if header missing, router would need to inspect each item — O(n) — which is fine for small requests but bad for huge payloads. Better fallback: require header OR accept but do best-effort and emit warning header.

anna: We should avoid breaking clients. Proposal: start by accepting mixed dims but reply with `X-Embed-Compat: mixed-dims-warning` for a deprecation window, then after 30 days make header recommended.

jen: Console UX: show a "split preview" in request inspector that shows how many shards we'd create and an estimated cost/latency delta. Also surface the deprecation warning (if any) in the request timeline.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: routing-optimizer v2 rolled out to staging (rd-embeds).

mike: Edge case: when we shard, quota accounting becomes tricky. If a customer has per-route quotas, do we count shards against the same quota and same route? If we route shards to multiple backends that can bypass per-route limits. Not acceptable.

devon: We should pin shards to the same customer pool/route to preserve quota semantics. If pinned pool is full, we can either queue or fail.

anna: Another practical problem: many clients base64 encode arrays, which inflates bytes. We need to document `max_payload_bytes` and recommended payload formats (binary/ndarray) to reduce surprises.

mike: Draft numbers: `max_items_per_request = 5000`, `max_payload_bytes = 10_485_760` (10MiB). If > max, return 413 with `X-Embed-Expectations` header pointing to docs and a suggested split strategy.

devon: For automatic splitting: suggest we implement a deterministic shard algorithm: group by dim, then within same-dim group split into chunks of N items not exceeding bytes threshold. Keep stable ordering so checksums match.

anna: Telemetry additions: include `embed.request.shard_sizes` (array) and `embed.request.most_common_dim`. Keep sample rate default 1% for huge requests to avoid high-cardinality costs.

mike: I'll open the telemetry PR tonight. I'll add a schema doc and event names.

jen: I'll mock the console split-preview UI in Figma and wire a quick prototype to the request inspector. Will include toggles: "auto-split" (on/off) and "require-dims-header" (rollout).

sre-bot: Alert: 413 errors for /v1/embeddings up 3x in last 6h. Top offenders: sdk-js@older versions sending base64 payloads.

anna: Good catch. Let's ship a temporary mitigation: emit `X-Deprecated-Warning` header for large requests with a link, and a short public docs blurb on recommended payload formats.

mike: Agree. Mitigation plan: telemetry PR + header + docs update. Devon — can you draft the router sharding prototype?

devon: Yep. I'll prototype simple dim-based grouping + max-bytes chunker. Will add a feature flag on the router so we can toggle in staging.

anna: Thanks all. I'll track this as an eng-platform work item and loop in support to notify customers.

jen: tagging @mike @devon for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
